served.stem: Adenylyl cyclase makes the second messenger cAMP. What is its starting material?
served.bankWhy: cAMP is adenosine monophosphate closed into a ring, and it is cut straight out of ATP by adenylyl cyclase. Keep the pairs together: adenylyl cyclase takes ATP to cAMP, guanylyl cyclase takes GTP to cGMP, phospholipase C takes PIP2 to IP3 plus DAG. Match the first letter of the enzyme to the first letter of its substrate.

answer.line: cAMP is AMP closed into a ring, cut straight out of ATP. Adenylyl points to adenine, so the enzyme starts from ATP.

steps: Read the name. Adenylyl points to adenine, and cAMP is cyclic adenosine monophosphate.
The enzyme takes ATP, pops off two phosphates as pyrophosphate, and closes the ring: cAMP.
GTP sits upstream. GTP on the G protein switches the enzyme on, but the enzyme's raw material is ATP.

choices.note: PIP2 is the membrane lipid that phospholipase C splits into IP3 and DAG, a neighbor pathway.
GTP feeds guanylyl cyclase, which makes cGMP. GTP on the G protein switches adenylyl cyclase on, which is why it pulls.
Adenylyl cyclase cuts cAMP straight out of ATP.
Phosphocreatine is muscle's quick reserve for remaking ATP. It is not a signaling substrate.
Cholesterol is the raw material for steroid hormones, not for a cyclic nucleotide.
